[P1] Distinguish a completed null result from an absent result

`JacksonSerDes.serialize(null)` returns null, so a successful async `Void` step leaves `unsavedResult` null even though its completion future has been completed. While SUCCEED is unanswered, `get()` therefore falls through to storage, where the operation is missing or still STARTED, and throws instead of returning null. This also affects the `waitForCallback` submitter when async semantics are configured globally. The same sentinel allows `onCheckpointComplete()` to fire a second end hook. Track local completion independently of the nullable payload, and cover a null/Void result with SUCCEED held pending.
